minutes.headline: Finance Committee heard Town Hall/Ritter and Marshall Park plans, deferred budget work, and put schools on for next week.
minutes.summary: The committee heard presentations from the Municipal Building Design Committee on a new town hall plus Ritter renovation, and from the Parks Commission on a three-phase Marshall Park project, both to be funded by excluded debt. The town manager said the budget, free cash transfers and capital plan remain in flux, and that a citizens' petition for a roughly two-million-dollar override was verified today. The chair cancelled next week's meeting slot for town budget work, scheduled the school committee for next week, and held a public hearing with comment on budget ownership, fees and cutting items.

public_comment.topic: Asked what effect not contributing to OPEB this year would have on the bond rating, given possible large debt exclusions.
Asked whether the per-household cost was per year or per month, and referenced back-of-napkin override figures.
Asked how much had been spent so far on the Marshall Park project design.
Explained school choice seat decisions, teacher cuts reducing capacity, and class-size concerns.
Urged the town manager to own the budget and bring forward her own budget rather than everyone's.
Urged chair to build own budget; suggested fees, park badges, school fees, cutting the cemetery capital item, and a cemetery corporation.
Opposed the town hall plan while acknowledging ADA need; raised the lost cap, PAC funding, storm water utility, employees and layoffs.
Asked for another public hearing, wanted override sponsors to explain breakdown, criticised unfunded school articles and select board's free cash use.
public_comment.stated_role: former resident and former committee member

public_comment.topic: Urged pursuing grants such as the ADA grant, and supported better accessible meeting space.
Agreed on grants; warned grants carry maintenance costs; urged raising fees.

budget_items.what_was_said: Presenter gave per-household annual costs for 30-year and 20-year bonds, declining over time, not net of expiring debt.

Capital item, special town meeting article, and ARPA funds paid for design; most ARPA was handed back.

School committee to present its budget at next week's (20th) meeting.
Possibility of added meetings the week after April 3 to be assessed on the 27th; votes and report on April 3 and 10.
Another public hearing to be planned, likely on the 27th or April 3.
Town manager to ask the print vendor whether text delivered on the 11th can be mailed by the 15th; warrant mailing goal is April 16.
Town manager to request the capital planning committee reconvene.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee took no votes; it heard presentations on a new town hall with a Ritter renovation and on a three-phase Marshall Park project, both planned as excluded debt.
The Marshall Park presentation covered phases, grants that had to be returned, a plan to reapply, and spending to date on design.
The town manager said a citizens' petition for an override was verified today, and that the budget, free cash transfers and capital plan are still in flux.
The chair cancelled next week's town budget meeting because budgets and articles are not final, and scheduled the School Committee to present on the 20th.
A public hearing drew comment on budget ownership, fees and the town hall plan; another hearing is planned for the 27th or April 3.

why_it_matters: The town hall and Marshall Park projects would be paid through excluded debt, which is added to the tax bill on top of the levy limit, so both could reach a resident's bill if voters approve them.
The verified override petition and unfinished town budget mean a possible override vote is still open, and the schools' budget presentation is the next place its size may become clearer.
watch_next: School Committee budget presentation at the March 20 meeting.
Votes and report on April 3 and 10; a second public hearing likely March 27 or April 3.
